turns.en: And so I started thinking about how would I make it so my agents could just automatically fix bugs for me while I sleep.
turns.zh: 所以我开始思考如何让我的智能体在我睡觉时自动为我修复 bug。

turns.en: And so that was the inspiration for some of our earlier experiments with building a more persistent bot. I think there were some ideas we took from there. Because I got so many questions like, how did you build Benny? How can I build my own? I think that inspired some of the thinking behind Grok Bot. Like, what if everybody could define one of their own bots, give it an identity, and give it things like its own computer plus routines and automations. So I have bots right now that, every time someone gives us feedback on Grok Bot, my bots automatically go off and fix them for me, and I just review their code.
turns.zh: 所以那就是我们早期一些实验的灵感来源——做一个更持久的机器人。我觉得我们从那里借鉴了一些想法。因为我收到太多问题，比如你是怎么做出 Benny 的？我怎么才能做出自己的？我觉得这启发了 Grok Bot 背后的一些思考。比如，如果每个人都能定义自己的机器人，给它一个身份，再给它自己的电脑、例行程序和自动化，会怎样？所以我现在有一些机器人，每当有人给 Grok Bot 反馈，我的机器人就会自动去帮我修，我只需要审阅它们的代码。

turns.en: So what's your job now? How's it changed?
turns.zh: 那你现在的工作是什么？它发生了怎样的变化？

turns.en: It's definitely become interesting as I'm almost like a manager for my digital colleagues. Yeah, so it's pretty interesting.
turns.zh: 确实变得很有意思，我几乎像是我的数字同事们的管理者。对，所以挺有意思的。

turns.en: It's actually remarkable how much of Grok Bot was built with Grok Bot, too. It's been a really cool feedback loop where these agents can self-triage issues. They can write code. And so they can connect to cloud agents. And I don't know if you have a demo of that, Lauren, that we wanted to show.
turns.zh: 其实很了不起的是，Grok Bot 有很大一部分也是用 Grok Bot 构建的。这是一个很酷的反馈循环：这些智能体能自己分诊问题，能写代码，还能连接到云端智能体。Lauren，我不知道你有没有那个我们想展示的演示。

turns.en: I do.
turns.zh: 我有。

turns.en: Ooh, I love these demos. This is so fun.
turns.zh: 哦，我喜欢这些演示。太好玩了。

turns.en: It's like the best way to explain something is to make it interactive.
turns.zh: 解释一件事最好的方式就是让它变得可交互。

turns.en: Exactly. You explain something and you're like, "Wow, I do have a demo pulled up. Let me just show you now how it actually works."
turns.zh: 没错。你解释一件事，然后你会想：“哇，我确实有个演示已经打开了。让我现在就给你看看它实际是怎么运作的。”

turns.en: Yeah, so I kind of asked my chief of staff already if there's any interesting bugs that we saw today. And it's found a few. You can also see I have X open on my bot's computer, just in case. But yeah, I can tell it to dispatch. So I have a team over here — sorry, a Grok Bot team. So each of them kind of is responsible for a different feature. And so now my chief of staff is going to send off those tasks to those agents. And in a minute we'll see a bunch of messages that it'll send to my different team members. And then they'll go off and actually work on those tasks. And then at the end of it I'll get a pull request that I can review. I'll get videos. I'll get a screenshot. Um, and yeah. So here's another example where this is like one of my engineering team agents. And I think this is almost like a feature that's not super obvious, but if you set up cloud agents on Cursor, your Grok Bot bots can actually kick them off.
turns.zh: 对，所以我先问了我的幕僚长，今天有没有看到什么有意思的 bug。它找到了几个。你也能看到，我在我的机器人的电脑上开着 X，以防万一。不过对，我可以让它去派发任务。所以我这边有一个团队——抱歉，是一个 Grok Bot 团队。它们每个负责一个不同的功能。现在我的幕僚长会把这些任务发给那些智能体。过一会儿我们就会看到它发给我不同团队成员的一堆消息。然后它们就会去实际处理那些任务。最后我会收到一个可以审阅的拉取请求。我会收到视频，会收到截图。嗯，对。这里还有一个例子，这是我工程团队的一个智能体。我觉得这几乎算是一个不太明显的功能，但如果你在 Cursor 上设置了云端智能体，你的 Grok Bot 机器人其实可以启动它们。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: So like here, we have a cloud agent that's running with its own computer that this agent is managing. And so it's got a bunch of things in flight already. So I have a bunch of PRs to review later.
turns.zh: 比如这里，我们有一个云端智能体，带着它自己的电脑在运行，由这个智能体来管理。所以它已经有一堆任务在进行中了。所以我稍后有一堆 PR 要审阅。

turns.en: I think there's something really exciting about the future of software development here, too, where it's really like talking to and working with a bunch of agents that are doing specific tasks, and then you kind of just step back and become the manager of them, and it sort of feels like that vision's coming true in a really fun way here. So, yeah.
turns.zh: 我觉得这里也展现了软件开发未来非常令人兴奋的一面：你实际上是在和一群执行特定任务的智能体交谈、协作，然后你退后一步，成为它们的管理者，感觉那个愿景正在以一种非常有趣的方式成真。所以，对。

turns.en: That's amazing. And I see here it's a bunch of cat photos.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我看到这里是一堆猫咪照片。

turns.en: Oh, yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，对。

turns.en: So, all your agents are actual cats.
turns.zh: 所以，你所有的智能体都是真正的猫。

turns.en: Yeah, I just love cats, so I decided to give them silly profile pictures just to personalize my Grok Bot a little bit. I mean, the default Grok Bot avatars are super cute as well. And I added these before we added those, but it's just having a bit of fun, you know?
turns.zh: 对，我就是喜欢猫，所以决定给它们一些傻乎乎的头像，让我的 Grok Bot 稍微个性化一点。我是说，默认的 Grok Bot 头像也超级可爱。而且我是在我们加上那些之前就加了这些，不过就是图个乐子，你懂的。

turns.en: Yeah. Roshan, you hinted towards something that is a trend that is of course happening with the future of agent AI coding, and Cursor has been at the front and center of seeing all of this happen. More and more code is getting automated and is done by these agents. And so, as a human, you become this puppeteer of agents who are handling all these tasks for you. I know that's a world that you're particularly excited about. Can you share a little bit more? Why are you excited about that? What does that actually unlock at maybe the human level that people in the mainstream audience might not realize?
turns.zh: 对。Roshan，你刚才暗示了一个趋势，这当然是智能体 AI 编程未来正在发生的事，而 Cursor 一直处在见证这一切的最前沿。越来越多的代码被自动化，由这些智能体来完成。所以作为人类，你成了操控这些智能体的木偶师，它们替你处理所有这些任务。我知道那是你特别兴奋的一个世界。你能多分享一点吗？你为什么对此感到兴奋？在人类层面，它究竟解锁了什么，可能是主流受众没有意识到的？

turns.en: Yeah, totally. I think if I had to pick one word, it would be efficiency. I think there are so many ideas in people's heads, regardless of role again. Like, I have so many product ideas I want to build into Cursor. And it's the limiting factor. Like, there's always some bottleneck in that idea-to-existence pipeline. And so I think the promise of being able to throw fleets of agents at these problems, and then have them produce things that are really high quality and sort of align with the taste that I would myself put into a product — that's the vision, right? That's sort of the dream. It's like being able to go from thought to existence. So to me that's the thing to work towards: can we build these things in a way where, whether I'm managing a bunch of agents or asking agents to manage other agents or working with Lauren's agents or whatever that looks like, we're able to really shorten, compress, compress, compress that cycle more and more. And I think if you look at the evolution of Cursor as a company, that's sort of how we've built ourselves towards that future, by continuously introducing more and more agent tools and complexity there. So, yeah, I think that's the vision and we're excited for it.
turns.zh: 对，完全同意。我觉得如果只能选一个词，那就是效率。我觉得人们脑子里有太多想法了，不管是什么角色。比如，我有太多想构建进 Cursor 的产品想法。而这就是限制因素。从想法到存在这条流水线上总会有某个瓶颈。所以我认为，能够把成群的智能体投向这些问题，然后让它们产出真正高质量、并且符合我自己会放进产品里的那种品味的东西——那就是愿景，对吧？那就是梦想。就像能够从想法直达存在。所以对我来说，这就是要努力的方向：我们能不能以这样的方式构建这些东西，无论是我管理一群智能体，还是让智能体去管理其他智能体，还是和 Lauren 的智能体协作，或者不管是什么形式，我们都能真正地缩短、压缩、再压缩那个周期。而且我觉得如果你看 Cursor 作为一家公司的演进，那在某种程度上就是我们朝着那个未来构建自己的方式——不断引入越来越多的智能体工具和复杂性。所以，对，我认为那就是愿景，我们对此很兴奋。

turns.en: And then how has it changed the software engineering team? What differences from when you started working at Cursor to how it is now?
turns.zh: 那它如何改变了软件工程团队？从你刚开始在 Cursor 工作到现在，有什么不同？

turns.en: I think the way I see engineers' roles evolve in the agent world is, you know, like I mentioned, you're sort of an engineering manager for your agents. But I think a big part of our responsibility now as engineers is also to keep the codebase in a condition where product managers and designers can contribute high-quality code.
turns.zh: 我觉得在我看来，工程师的角色在智能体世界里是这样演变的：就像我提到的，你某种程度上是你那些智能体的工程经理。但我认为，作为工程师，我们现在很大一部分责任也是让代码库保持在一个产品经理和设计师都能贡献高质量代码的状态。

turns.en: And that's something I talk a lot about on Twitter as well, which is investing in refactoring, rewriting, even rewriting your code base so that agents can really thrive even if they're not very smart agents sometimes. Things like encoding your rules and your style guides into actual lint rules or hard constraints that fail CI so that again, the big unlock is as an engineer, I can empower so many other people to do things that they couldn't do before.
turns.zh: 这也是我在 Twitter 上经常谈论的一点，就是投资于重构、重写，甚至重写你的代码库，以便智能体能够真正蓬勃发展，即使它们有时并不是很聪明的智能体。比如将你的规则和风格指南编码成实际的 lint 规则或硬性约束，让 CI 失败，这样再次强调，最大的突破是作为一名工程师，我可以赋能许多其他人去做他们以前做不到的事情。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And I can do things that I couldn't do before as well because I've done a lot of big refactors and migrations at Cursor and I did them mostly by myself, like with one other person.
turns.zh: 而且我也能做以前做不到的事情，因为我在 Cursor 做了很多大型重构和迁移，而且我主要是自己做的，就像和另一个人一起。

turns.en: Agents.
turns.zh: 智能体。

turns.en: Yeah, all the cat agents were just going wild and I converted a bunch of stuff, which would have taken me or a team of engineers months or even years to finish.
turns.zh: 是的，所有的猫智能体都疯狂地工作，我转换了一堆东西，这本来需要我或一个工程师团队花费数月甚至数年才能完成。

turns.en: Wow, that's incredible. And as an outsider's perspective, you might think, 'Okay, now that agents can do all this coding, what's the role of a software engineer?' And if you actually look at what's happening on the ground, there's more demand than ever for more and more of these engineers. And it's probably towards something that you hinted. Now that you can build software with the thought to execution timeline is getting so condensed, we just now get something like Grok Bot that started off as that something you guys are building, and then you can use Grok Bot to now build Grok Bot and put it out into commercial production. Is that also what you're seeing just as a trend happen more and more?
turns.zh: 哇，那太不可思议了。从外人的角度来看，你可能会想，‘好吧，既然智能体能做所有这些编码工作，软件工程师的角色是什么？’而如果你实际看看实地发生的情况，对这些工程师的需求比以往任何时候都多。这可能指向你暗示的某些东西。现在你可以构建软件，从想法到执行的时间线变得如此压缩，我们现在有了像 Grok Bot 这样的东西，它最初是你们正在构建的东西，然后你可以使用 Grok Bot 来构建 Grok Bot 并将其投入商业生产。这也是你看到的趋势吗，越来越频繁地发生？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, I think the time to prototype ideas has gone down a bunch, and so it's really quick to test things. I think we've been able, like the team behind Grok Bot has been able to move incredibly quickly just because of these tools getting better, and obviously the model's getting better is a huge component of that. And so, yeah, I think to bring it to the Grok Bot side of things, the motivation there is really around how can we make this product more and more helpful for folks. As far as the trend, I think this is going to get easier. I think there's still a really strong role for people to play in all that, too, right? Whether it's the taste argument or some other combination like that, but yeah, I think it's just ideas are abound, and it's just going to be exciting to see more and more of them come to reality.
turns.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为原型化想法的时间大大减少了，所以测试东西非常快。我认为我们能够——就像 Grok Bot 背后的团队能够以令人难以置信的速度前进，只是因为这些工具变得更好，显然模型变得更好是其中的一个巨大组成部分。所以，是的，我认为就 Grok Bot 方面而言，那里的动机真的是围绕如何让这个产品对人们越来越有帮助。至于趋势，我认为这会变得更容易。我认为人们在所有这些中仍然扮演着非常重要的角色，对吧？无论是品味论证还是其他类似的组合，但是的，我认为想法是丰富的，看到越来越多的想法成为现实将令人兴奋。

turns.en: Wow, that's so
turns.zh: 哇，那太

turns.en: Yeah, the sort of analogy or metaphor that I personally like a lot is this idea that so, I like food. Yeah. I'm a big lover of food, and I kind of think of my agents as sort of like a kitchen a Michelin kitchen is what I call it. And so, like, maybe my role has sort of changed in that maybe I'm not cooking all the food myself anymore, but I have a team of bots and agents that are that I've sort of hired, right? And I've trained through skills or refactoring to do good code the way that I would have done it. And so my role is becoming more like a head chef, right? Like I maybe assemble a plate of the food. I own the quality control, but if you invest a lot in having like early capable team of agents, you can just do so much more. And now think about that like with every engineer in your team can have one of these teams behind them. You can really you can solve a lot more problems, you know, you can build more features. Not all of them should be built, but you have much more productivity and velocity.
turns.zh: 是的，我个人非常喜欢的一个类比或隐喻是这个想法，所以，我喜欢食物。是的。我是一个美食爱好者，我有点把我的智能体想象成一种厨房，我称之为米其林厨房。所以，也许我的角色有所改变，也许我不再自己烹饪所有的食物，但我有一队机器人和智能体，我有点像雇佣了他们，对吧？我通过技能或重构训练他们以我会做的方式写出好的代码。所以我的角色变得更像主厨，对吧？比如我可能组装一盘食物。我负责质量控制，但如果你大量投资于拥有早期有能力的智能体团队，你可以做更多的事情。现在想想，你团队中的每个工程师都可以拥有这样的团队在背后支持。你真的可以解决更多问题，你可以构建更多功能。不是所有的都应该被构建，但你有更高的生产力和速度。

turns.en: Yeah. I do like what you hinted about the internal culture of you actually build things, you test it out, and that the employees themselves at Cursor have a certain taste for what other engineers, what other product people, what other consumers like I guess in general would want to see exist. Do you have any hints that you can maybe share, okay if you don't, but of what might be coming up or even something that people are working on internally?
turns.zh: 是的。我确实喜欢你暗示的关于内部文化的东西，你实际构建东西，测试它，而且 Cursor 的员工本身对其他工程师、其他产品人员、其他消费者——我猜一般来说——希望看到存在的东西有一定的品味。你有没有什么提示可以分享，好吧，如果你没有的话，但关于可能即将出现的东西，甚至人们内部正在做的事情？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, we definitely want to make Grok Bot better. We launched this as a beta yesterday, and so tons of feedback coming in of all shapes and sizes. Our goal there is just to make this as helpful these assistants, these bots as helpful as we can. And so definitely going to continue investing there. Obviously really excited about the models getting better, too, and excited to be a part of that conversation and to have frontier models now. And so I think we're going to continue to just invest a bunch in that space. And then, you know, some more fun stuff to come, too. But I think overall like just very bullish on the future and the future of both coding agents, but also as general purpose agents. And I think it's going to be a really fun time. So.
turns.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我们肯定想让 Grok Bot 更好。我们昨天作为测试版推出了这个，所以大量的反馈从各种形状和大小涌来。我们的目标只是让这些助手、这些机器人尽可能有帮助。所以肯定会继续在那里投资。显然也对模型变得更好感到兴奋，并兴奋能成为对话的一部分，现在拥有前沿模型。所以我认为我们将继续在那个领域大量投资。然后，你知道，还有一些更有趣的东西要来。但我认为总体上只是对未来非常看好，无论是编码智能体的未来，还是通用智能体的未来。我认为这将是一个非常有趣的时期。所以。

turns.en: Definitely.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: Yeah, I'm personally really excited to see more performance and reliability as an engineer that is something that I care about a lot. But yeah, we have something like really interesting features that we're debating. You know, like actually one thing that I tried to hack I hacked into Grok Bot like in the early days was support for iMessage. You can actually text your bots. I don't know if we'll add it for Grok Bot, but I know it's like a common ask. So, we're definitely thinking about things like this where again, it's like the mental model is these are colleagues, right? So like how do you like your colleague is accessible not just through Slack, right? That you can text them, you can call them. So, it's interesting to kind of imagine a world where you have these always-on colleagues that you can talk to at any time from anywhere. And they're just off doing good work for you.
turns.zh: 是的，我个人非常兴奋地看到更多的性能和可靠性，作为一名工程师，这是我非常关心的。但是的，我们有一些真正有趣的功能正在讨论。你知道，实际上我在早期尝试破解过 Grok Bot，我破解了像 iMessage 的支持。你实际上可以给你的机器人发短信。我不知道我们是否会为 Grok Bot 添加它，但我知道这是一个常见的要求。所以，我们肯定在思考这样的事情，再次，心理模型是这些是同事，对吧？所以就像你希望你的同事不仅通过 Slack 可以联系，对吧？你可以给他们发短信，你可以打电话给他们。所以，想象一个世界，你有这些始终在线的同事，你可以随时随地从任何地方与他们交谈。他们只是在外为你做好工作。

turns.en: Oh my gosh, I can't wait to be able to text them or call them. I saw this meme where it's like my agents were talking to each other in their stand-up and they're like, 'Sorry, I was off like all weekend.' It's like, 'You're an agent.' Like, I don't know exactly what that means.
turns.zh: 哦我的天，我迫不及待想能够给他们发短信或打电话。我看到这个梗，就像我的智能体在站会上互相交谈，他们说，‘抱歉，我整个周末都休息了。’就像，‘你是个智能体。’就像，我不知道那到底是什么意思。

turns.en: Yeah, maybe we need agent PTO and agent fun time.
turns.zh: 是的，也许我们需要智能体带薪休假和智能体娱乐时间。

turns.en: PTO. Turn your computer off.
turns.zh: 带薪休假。把你的电脑关掉。

turns.en: Let's do it.
turns.zh: 让我们做吧。

turns.en: One last thing I did want to bring up because this is really impressive is you guys of course not just working on Grok Bot, not just working on the application layer, but also on the model layer. And Grok 4.6, the benchmarks came out on Cursor Bench 3.2 and were really impressive and I wanted to address them here on air while we still have time. You had Grok 4.6 extra high scored 70.8% at an average cost of 2.81 per task.
turns.zh: 最后我想提一件事，因为这真的很令人印象深刻，你们当然不仅在开发 Grok Bot，不仅在应用层工作，还在模型层工作。而 Grok 4.6 在 Cursor Bench 3.2 上的基准测试结果出来了，真的令人印象深刻，我想在我们还有时间的时候在这里提一下。你们的 Grok 4.6 extra high 得分 70.8%，平均每任务成本 2.81。

ts.sec: Efficiency and Cost of AI Models

turns.en: For context, Fable 5 Max scored 70.5%, but at $17.32. This is a huge change. How does this model maybe change how the everyday consumer actually interacts with agents, with AI as a whole?
turns.zh: 补充一下背景：Fable 5 Max 得分 70.5%，但成本是 17.32 美元。这是个巨大的变化。这个模型可能会如何改变普通消费者与智能体、乃至与整个 AI 的互动方式？

turns.en: Yeah. So this is definitely very top of mind for me, because I think about this a lot since I work at Cursor. I have unlimited tokens, so I can just go crazy with token maxing. But obviously a lot of our customers and our users are more cost conscious. So personally, what I'm most excited about is this idea that you have a very efficient model that is as good as some of the other big models but at a fraction of the cost. And I feel like that's a very important topic that a lot of leaders and engineers are having right now, which is the rising cost of using AI. So I think Grok 4.6 is a really interesting choice in that discussion. Every company's going to have their own requirements, I suppose, for the type of model mix that they use. So I think Grok 4.6 makes a very compelling option. If you're considering between some of the bigger models, which are also extremely capable, but you want something a little bit cheaper, Grok is an excellent choice.
turns.zh: 是的。这确实是我非常关注的问题，因为我在 Cursor 工作，经常思考这件事。我有无限的 token，所以可以随便把 token 用到极致。但显然，我们的很多客户和用户对成本更敏感。所以对我个人来说，最让我兴奋的是：你有一个非常高效的模型，它和某些其他大模型一样好，但成本只是它们的一小部分。我觉得这是很多领导者和工程师现在都在讨论的重要话题，也就是使用 AI 的成本不断上升。所以我认为 Grok 4.6 在这场讨论中是一个很有意思的选择。每家公司对自己使用的模型组合大概都有自己的要求。所以我觉得 Grok 4.6 是一个非常有吸引力的选项。如果你在几个更大的模型之间考虑——它们也非常强大——但想要更便宜一些，Grok 就是个极好的选择。

turns.en: Yeah. It's like if you have a budget of 20 bucks to do all of your AI tasks, and the cost per task goes down, you can just do more tasks. And so I think the efficiency game is just such a fun one to play, because it feels like you can just do more — you can have more bots or write more code. And I think this is happening across the industry, which is very exciting, but just being able to do more things with the tokens is wildly cool to see. So yeah, I think we are investing a ton in efficiency, specifically because we think that's just a really great direction for these models to go in. And obviously intelligence matters a ton too, so we're excited about the results. The benchmark results are pretty cool.
turns.zh: 是啊。就像你有 20 美元的预算来做所有 AI 任务，如果每个任务的成本下降，你就能做更多任务。所以我觉得效率这场游戏玩起来特别有意思，因为感觉你能做更多事——可以有更多机器人，或者写更多代码。我觉得这正在整个行业发生，非常令人兴奋；光是能用这些 token 做更多事情，就已经酷得不行了。所以是的，我们在效率上投入了大量精力，正是因为我们觉得这对这些模型来说是个非常好的方向。当然，智能本身也极其重要，所以我们对结果很兴奋。基准测试的结果挺酷的。

turns.en: Yeah, that was really cool to see. And now I'm super excited specifically about lowering costs for such a great model. It provides better capabilities for startups that maybe don't have the same amount of resources, or even just indie hackers who want to experiment but can't be paying for all of their token costs out of pocket, because it's just getting a little bit crazy. So it's really starting to level the playing field, and I'm incredibly excited about what that actually means and what that looks like for the future and for all of your guys' products.
turns.zh: 是啊，看到这个真的很酷。现在我特别兴奋的是，这么出色的模型把成本降了下来。它为那些资源可能没那么多的初创公司提供了更好的能力，甚至对独立开发者也是如此——他们想实验，但没法自掏腰包支付所有 token 成本，因为那已经有点离谱了。所以这真的开始让竞争环境变得公平，我对这实际意味着什么、对未来以及对你们所有人的产品会是什么样子，感到无比兴奋。

turns.en: But Lauren, um, Roshan, really wanted to thank you guys for coming on MTS today and sharing more about Grok Bot, Grok 4.6, and all of the fun updates.
turns.zh: Lauren、Roshan，真的很感谢你们今天来到 MTS，分享关于 Grok Bot、Grok 4.6 以及所有这些有趣的更新。

turns.en: Thanks so much for having us. Yeah, it's super fun. And if you haven't tried Grok Bot, give it a shot. It's really great.
turns.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们。是啊，特别有意思。如果你还没试过 Grok Bot，去试试吧，真的很棒。

turns.en: I'll definitely have to give it a shot. Appreciate you guys for joining, and we'll be back with MTS.
turns.zh: 我一定得去试试。感谢你们参加，我们稍后回到 MTS。

Out-of-home advertising as easy to scale as digital. adquick.com. Arena, measuring AI performance in the real world. arena.ai.
turns.zh: 非常感谢 MTS 的赞助商。Blitzcy，面向企业代码库的自主软件开发，交付速度快 5 倍。blitzcy.com。AdQuick，让你的品牌成为广告牌。户外广告像数字广告一样容易规模化。adquick.com。Arena，在真实世界中衡量 AI 表现。arena.ai。

consensus.en: Grok Bot makes agents accessible to everyone by giving each bot its own computer and seamless tool integration.
consensus.zh: Grok Bot 通过为每个机器人提供自己的电脑和无缝的工具集成，让智能体对所有人可用。

consensus.en: Internal PMF across roles—ops, go-to-market, engineering—validated Grok Bot before public launch.
consensus.zh: 跨角色的内部 PMF——运营、市场、工程——在公开发布前验证了 Grok Bot。

consensus.en: Grok 4.6 matches top models on Cursor Bench at a fraction of the cost, democratizing AI access.
consensus.zh: Grok 4.6 在 Cursor Bench 上以极低成本匹配顶级模型，使 AI 访问民主化。

consensus.en: Engineers evolve into managers of agent fleets, focusing on codebase health and empowering others.
consensus.zh: 工程师演变为智能体团队的管理者，专注于代码库健康并赋能他人。

consensus.en: The future of software development is orchestrating fleets of specialized agents to compress idea-to-existence cycles.
consensus.zh: 软件开发的未来是编排专业化智能体团队，以压缩从想法到实现的周期。

consensus.en: Grok Bot was largely built with Grok Bot, demonstrating a powerful self-improving feedback loop.
consensus.zh: Grok Bot 很大程度上是用 Grok Bot 构建的，展示了强大的自我改进反馈循环。

contrarian.en: Agent UX for everyday tasks is broken; simplicity, not power, is the key design principle.
contrarian.zh: 日常任务的智能体用户体验是糟糕的；简洁而非强大才是关键设计原则。

contrarian.en: Engineers should invest in refactoring and rewriting codebases so even less capable agents can thrive.
contrarian.zh: 工程师应投资于重构和重写代码库，以便能力较弱的智能体也能茁壮成长。

contrarian.en: Rising AI costs make efficiency as critical as raw intelligence for frontier models.
contrarian.zh: AI 成本上升使得效率与原始智能同样关键，对于前沿模型而言。

contrarian.en: Agents should be treated like colleagues, not micromanaged tools—accessible anytime, anywhere.
contrarian.zh: 智能体应被视为同事，而非微观管理的工具——随时随地可访问。

contrarian.en: More software engineers are needed than ever, despite agents automating coding tasks.
contrarian.zh: 尽管智能体自动化了编码任务，但比以往任何时候都更需要更多软件工程师。

contrarian.en: Taste and quality control remain human roles as agents handle more execution.
contrarian.zh: 随着智能体处理更多执行，品味和质量控制仍是人类的角色。
